fields.description:
## Context / Problem

`import rebar` callers get a return value, not a terminal, so the first-class way to raise
a non-fatal warning is Python's dedicated **`warnings`** subsystem (not `logging`, which is
silent unless the app configures it, and which the brainstorm rejected). This story emits a
`warnings.warn` of a dedicated category from single-ticket library functions when the
detector fires. Depends on the detector (`cross_session_warning_for`, merged) and the
reducer clearing (merged): a ticket not `in_progress` has no holder, so the detector returns
`None` and nothing is emitted.

## Approach

Add a small new module `src/rebar/_lib_warn.py` defining
`class CrossSessionWarning(UserWarning)` and one best-effort emit helper
`emit_cross_session_warning(ticket_id, *, repo_root=None, stacklevel=3)`; re-export the
category as `rebar.CrossSessionWarning` from the package so callers can filter/escalate it
with stdlib `warnings` filters.

The helper mirrors the CLI's `_maybe_warn_cross_session`
(`src/rebar/_cli/_execute.py:60`): it imports and calls the merged detector
`cross_session_warning_for(ticket_id, repo_root=repo_root)` and, when it returns a non-`None`
string, calls `warnings.warn(msg, CrossSessionWarning, stacklevel=stacklevel)`; when it
returns `None` it does nothing. Two properties are load-bearing:

- **Best-effort — never breaks the call.** The whole body is wrapped in
  `try/except Exception: pass` (the detector performs a state read that can fail on
  corrupt/absent/locked state); the underlying library operation always proceeds and no
  warning is emitted on failure.
- **Re-entrancy-guarded.** The merged detector
  (`src/rebar/_commands/cross_session.py:44`) itself calls the public
  `rebar._lib_reads.show_ticket`, so instrumenting `show_ticket` with a naive emit would
  recurse without bound. A module-level `contextvars.ContextVar` flag
  (`_EMITTING`, default `False`) makes the helper a no-op while an emit is already in
  progress on the current context: the helper returns immediately if the flag is set,
  otherwise sets it (saving the token), runs, and resets it in a `finally`. Thus the
  detector's internal `show_ticket` read emits nothing and exactly one warning fires per
  top-level call. The detector is **not** modified. `stacklevel=3` attributes the warning
  to the caller of the public library function (user → public fn → helper → warn), not to
  rebar-internal frames.

Each single-ticket public library entry point calls
`emit_cross_session_warning(ticket_id, repo_root=repo_root)` **before** returning (and, for
writes, before performing the mutation, so the holder is read pre-mutation — matching the
CLI/MCP surfaces). **No return type changes** — the warning rides the `warnings` channel.

Functions to cover, at their actual definition sites (public names re-exported from
`src/rebar/__init__.py`):

- Reads — `_lib_reads.py`: `show_ticket` (`:40`), `deps` (`:172`).
- Writes — `_lib_writes.py`: `transition` (`:272`), `reopen` (`:455`).
- Mutations — `_lib_mutations.py`: `comment` (`:55`), `edit_ticket` (`:147`) (public name is
  **`edit_ticket`**, not `edit`), `link` (`:181`), `unlink` (`:205`), `tag` (`:221`),
  `untag` (`:234`), `archive` (`:247`).
- Gates — `_lib_gates.py`: `set_file_impact` (`:129`), `declare_no_file_impact` (`:141`),
  `clarity_check` (`:35`), `check_ac` (`:61`), `quality_check` (`:75`). Unlike the MCP
  surface (S4), which deferred `check_ac`/`quality_check`/`declare_no_file_impact` because a
  field would change those handlers' return shapes, the library emit changes no return
  type, so these are covered here for full parity with the CLI allowlist.

`link`/`unlink` take two endpoints (`id1, id2, relation`); the warning is computed for the
**primary endpoint `id1`** only, matching CLI (S3) and MCP (S4). Bulk reads
(`list_tickets`, `search`, `ready`, `next_batch`) do **not** warn. `claim` is excluded: it
raises `ConcurrencyError` on an `in_progress` ticket before any warning path.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_lib_warn.py` (**new**) — `CrossSessionWarning(UserWarning)` + best-effort,
  re-entrancy-guarded `emit_cross_session_warning`.
- `src/rebar/__init__.py` — re-export `CrossSessionWarning` (import + `__all__`).
- `src/rebar/_lib_reads.py` — emit in `show_ticket`, `deps`.
- `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` — emit in `transition`, `reopen` (before the mutation).
- `src/rebar/_lib_mutations.py` — emit in `comment`, `edit_ticket`, `link` (`id1`),
  `unlink` (`id1`), `tag`, `untag`, `archive` (before the mutation).
- `src/rebar/_lib_gates.py` — emit in `set_file_impact`, `declare_no_file_impact`,
  `clarity_check`, `check_ac`, `quality_check` (before the mutation, for the writes).
- `docs/reuse-surface.md` — document `rebar.CrossSessionWarning` and single-ticket emission
  (bulk reads excluded).

## Testing

Tier: **in-process unit test** with stdlib `warnings` capture (`pytest.warns` /
`warnings.catch_warnings(record=True)`) — the mechanism is entirely in-process
(test-design §3 pure/validation path). Real temporary tracker; acting session via
`REBAR_SESSION_ID` (monkeypatch). Claim as holder A, then act as B.

- B against A-held ticket: `rebar.show_ticket(<id>)` and `rebar.comment(<id>, "x")` each emit
  one `CrossSessionWarning` naming holder `A`; the write still applies.
- Write + two-endpoint: `rebar.transition(<id>, "in_progress", "closed")` and
  `rebar.link(<id1>, <id2>, ...)` (holder A on `id1`) each emit one warning for `id1`.
- Negative control (same session A): no `CrossSessionWarning` emitted.
- Bulk exclusion: `rebar.list_tickets()` / `rebar.ready()` as B emit none.
- Unset-id silence: `REBAR_SESSION_ID` unset → `rebar.show_ticket(<id>)` emits none.
- Category precision: emitted warning is `isinstance(..., rebar.CrossSessionWarning)`.
- Re-entrancy: exactly one warning per top-level `show_ticket` despite the detector's
  internal `show_ticket` read.
- Best-effort: monkeypatch `cross_session_warning_for` to raise → the call returns normally,
  no warning.
- Defect-seeded (mutation teeth): negate the `msg is not None` guard / target the wrong
  endpoint → warn/silence assertions go RED.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar.show_ticket(<id>)` and `rebar.comment(<id>, ...)` each emit exactly one
  `rebar.CrossSessionWarning` naming holder `A` as session B against an A-held ticket
  (checked by a `pytest.warns` test under `make test`).
- [ ] `rebar.transition(<id>, "in_progress", "closed")` and `rebar.link(<id1>, <id2>, ...)`
  (endpoint `id1`), as B against A-held `id1`, each emit one `CrossSessionWarning` naming
  holder `A` for `id1` (checked by `pytest.warns` assertions).
- [ ] Negative control: acting as session A, no `CrossSessionWarning` is emitted (checked by
  `catch_warnings(record=True)` asserting none of that category).
- [ ] `rebar.list_tickets()` and `rebar.ready()` as B emit no `CrossSessionWarning` for A's
  `in_progress` ticket (checked by a bulk-exclusion assertion).
- [ ] With `REBAR_SESSION_ID` unset, `rebar.show_ticket(<id>)` emits none (checked by an
  unset-id assertion).
- [ ] The emitted warning is an instance of `rebar.CrossSessionWarning` subclassing
  `UserWarning` (checked by an `isinstance` assertion).
- [ ] Exactly one `CrossSessionWarning` per top-level `rebar.show_ticket(<id>)` despite the
  detector's internal read — the re-entrancy guard holds (checked by asserting the
  recorded count for that category is 1).
- [ ] Best-effort: when `cross_session_warning_for` raises, the library call returns
  normally and emits no `CrossSessionWarning` (checked by a monkeypatch-to-raise test).
- [ ] `docs/reuse-surface.md` documents `rebar.CrossSessionWarning` and the single-ticket
  emission (checked: `grep -n "CrossSessionWarning" docs/reuse-surface.md` matches).
